mechanism: Both drugs increase serum potassium through different mechanisms (aldosterone antagonism and neprilysin inhibition reducing natriuretic peptide degradation), creating synergistic hyperkalemia risk, particularly in patients with renal impairment or diabetes.
action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function regularly; consider potassium-sparing agent alternatives or dose reduction if potassium levels exceed 5.5 mEq/L; patient education on dietary potassium restriction is essential.
